anyOf.description:
One value for `pick` among `options` (each said by the matching `labels` entry, else by
itself): what a host offers with its own picker — the platform's select on touch screens —
in place of the chart's drawn list. No pointer intent runs it.

Drag across the node to select a range along a scale: `axis` `x` or `y`, the scale of that
name unless `scale` says otherwise. Continuous scales write `<brush>.lo` / `<brush>.hi`
(data units); band scales write the keyset `<brush>` of the bands covered. Both set
`<brush>.active`; a click without a drag clears the brush.
Press or drag on the node to set `scrub` to the data value under the pointer along `axis`
(through the scale of that name, or `scale`) — sliders, time scrubbers.

min.description:
Keep the value at or above / below these (numbers or expressions, read when the scene
resolves): a range's low thumb stops at the high one's value.

step.description: Snap to multiples of this step (0 = continuous).

Action.description: What an intent does: set or toggle a signal, fire a program event, or enter a chapter.

param.description: The parameter bound to the activating datum's key (`{c}` in names, a signal in expressions).

Derived.description:
A derived table: `from` + ops, each op a small JSON object interpreted by the engine
(`filter`, `derive`, `aggregate`, `sort`, `top`, `bin`, `window`, `join`, `pivot`, `unpivot`,
`interpolate`, and layout algorithms like `stack`, `pie`, `treemap`, `beeswarm`, …).

GenColumn.description: One generated column: its name and its expression.

Generate.description:
A generated table: `rows` rows; each column an expression over the row, evaluated in order —
`d.i` is the row number and `d.<name>` any column before it — with `rand(key, stream)` and
`randn(key, stream)` for seeded randomness (the same rows on every platform). `keep` names
the columns the table ends up with (default: all); the others are working values.

align.description: Cross-axis alignment: `start | center | end | stretch` (default stretch).

padding.description:
Padding `[top, right, bottom, left]`; CSS shorthand accepted on input: `12`, `[12]`,
`[vertical, horizontal]`, `[top, horizontal, bottom]`.

type.description:
`stack` (default: children share the box), `rows`, `columns`, `grid` (equal cells, `columns`
across; a repeat fills one cell per item), or `flow` (resolved nodes left to right by their
size, wrapping at the box edge; a repeat's nodes flow too).

wrap.description:
`columns` only: in a box narrower than this (px), the children stack as rows instead, each
an equal share of the height (their widths dropped) — two charts side by side on a desktop,
one above the other on a phone.

every.description: Seconds between refreshes (poll), or 0 for push.

hash.description: Content hash of the package (pins exact behaviour, P1).

source.description: Inline JS source (dev) — published bundles carry bytecode chunks instead.

PaddingInput.description: What `padding` accepts on input (CSS shorthand): one number, or 1–4 numbers.

chapters.description: Parameterized sub-programs entered by an event with a key (chapters, drill-down).

Prop.description: A property value: a literal JSON value, or an expression (`{"expr": "…"}` or `"=…"`).

anyOf.description:
One child per group of rows: `{ "groups": "points", "by": "series" }`; inside, `"@group"` is
that group's rows and `d` its first row.

One child per tick of a scale: `{ "ticks": "y", "count": 5 }`; `d.value`, `d.label`. The
count is a hint (0 or none: from the axis length), and may be an expression — so many ticks
as labels of their measured width fit along the axis.
One child per entry of a categorical/colour scale's domain: `d.value`, `d.ink`, `d.index`.

domain.description: `{"data": table, "field": col}`, `{"data", "expr"}`, a literal array, or `{"values": [...]}`.

exponent.description: `pow` only: values map through `sign(x)·|x|^exponent` (default 1, linear; `sqrt` is pow 0.5).

range.description:
`"width"`, `"height"`, `"-height"` (inverted), `[a, b]` (numbers or expressions), a palette
token (`"$categorical"`), or a list of inks.

type.description:
`linear | log | sqrt | pow | symlog | time | band | point | ordinal | quantize | quantile |
threshold | sequential | diverging | categorical | piecewise`

clock.description:
A clock signal: its value runs at this rate (units per second) while a settled scene reads
it — a globe that turns, a slow drift — and pauses during transitions, off screen and for
reduced motion. Resolving outside a running view (bake, render, goldens) sees its default.

control.description: A host-bound control, if any (`slider`, `toggle`, `select`) with its parameters.

type.description: `num | str | bool | key | keyset | range | point | json`

SizeSpec.description:
A size along one axis: px, `"auto"` (measured content), `"fill"` / `{"fill": weight}`, `"30%"`,
or an expression over the parent box in px (`{"expr": "min(260, box.w - 24)"}`).

Source.description: A data source. The engine never fetches (P10): `url` sources become requests the host fulfils.

oneOf.description: A URL the host fetches (CSV or JSON by extension or `format`).
Provided by the host at runtime (a data slot, docs/12-delivery.md).

Inline GeoJSON (a FeatureCollection): a geo source — a table of feature ids + properties,
and geometry the engine projects through a `geo` coordinate system.
A built-in atlas (`"countries"`, `"admin1"`, …) from the runtime or an atlas package.

A vector-tile archive (PMTiles v3) by URL. Never fetched whole: the engine asks the host for
byte ranges — the header and directories, then the tiles the visible views need at their
zoom (`Request::Range`). Drawn by `tiles` template nodes. [`AUTO_TILES`] (`"auto"`) asks the
build for an archive cut to the document's own cameras ([`tiles_file`]).

A font file (TrueType/OpenType) by URL, fetched like any source: its families join every
text's fallback chain, so labels in other scripts (Hebrew, Arabic, CJK) find their glyphs.

Rows the engine generates: synthetic data too big to write down (simulations, load tests,
procedural datasets) as a few expressions instead of millions of values.

id.description: Geo sources: the feature property holding the id (default `id`, else the feature's own id).

key.description: Key column(s): the identity of each row (P3).

live.description: Live updates: how the host should refresh this source.

rows.description:
Where a JSON response keeps its rows: a dotted path to the array of records (`data`,
`results.items`) — web APIs wrap their rows with paging and metadata.

sample.description:
Slots: rows shown until the host provides the data (design previews, tests, a published
chart's static fallback), as columns or records. They also say which columns the host's
data must have.

narration.description: Narration for the host (cards, captions, video subtitles) and an anchor key.

set.description: Signal assignments while in this state (values or `{"expr"}`).

TBackdrop.description:
A group's backdrop: a (rounded) box behind whatever the group draws, sized to it once layout is
done — so a card grows with its text, and morphs when the text changes. Keyed `backdrop`.

fit.description:
`content` (default) hugs the content; `width` spans the group's box across and hugs the
content's height (a card of fixed width).

padding.description: Space around the content: a number, or `[top, right, bottom, left]`.

radius.description: Corner radius (px or a number token).

anyOf.description: Fit keys (node keys under the view) or a bbox in content units, with padding px.

explore.description:
Free exploration (drag to pan, wheel/pinch to zoom) relative to the fit, kept in the
signals `<explore>.x`, `.y` (content centre) and `.zoom` (× the fit's zoom).

max_zoom.description: How far exploration zooms in, × the fit's zoom (default 64).

min_zoom.description: How far it zooms out, × the fit's zoom (default 0.5).

oneOf.description: Points from the rows of `from` (a table name, or `"@group"` for the current group's rows).
An SVG path string (literal or expression).

A feature of a geo source, projected through the enclosing geo coordinate system. Without
`source` (inside a `tiles` layer template): the current tile feature's geometry.

hit.description:
Where the pointer finds the instances: `marks` (the default), each mark and a few px around
it; or `line`, anywhere along the line through them in row order, within `reach` px of it,
finding the instance nearest to where it meets the line — a line's value wherever it's
hovered or tapped, however far apart its points are.

instance_key.description:
Per-instance key (an expression over the row). Separate from the node's own `key`: the
instances node keeps one identity, each instance another.

instance_opacity.description: Per-instance opacity (an expression over the row); the node's own `opacity` multiplies it.

lod.description:
Level of detail, for rows beyond what one frame can draw (millions): the rows are indexed
once into a pyramid of tiles and each frame draws only the tiles the camera shows — a
seeded, density-preserving sample of the rows in view, as many as `points` allows, every
row once they fit. Rows sit at their `x`/`y` in the node's own coordinates (indexed once, so
they read the row only); a transform or a view's camera above maps them to the screen.
`from` may also name a point archive (a `tiles` source written by the publish compiler).

proto.description: `circle | square | diamond | triangle | cross | star | rect`

r.description:
Radius (symbol prototypes), px; default: the theme's `point.radius`. Not `size`, which is
the node's layout size.

reach.description: How far from the line (`hit: line`) the pointer still finds it, px; default 16.

TLod.description: How an `instances` node with `lod` samples its rows.

budget.description:
Rows per tile of the index at average density (default 2048): how finely the rows are
cut up (smaller: more, lighter tiles to fetch).

points.description:
The most rows one frame draws (default 150,000): a view holding more draws a uniform
sample of them this size, a view holding fewer draws every one. It's for the document's
own size: a smaller view draws its share of it (by area, at least a fifth), so the sample
keeps the same density per pixel on a phone.

link.description:
A URL this element links to (a data credit's licence page, a source): hosts make it
clickable and announce it as a link; vector exports keep it.

number.description: A number that counts when animated: `{ "value": expr, "format": ",.1f" }`.

offset.description: Shift from `at` in screen px (labels beside points under a zooming camera).

contain.description:
Keep the label inside the canvas: after layout it's nudged back in, only as far as needed
(the last tick label of an axis, a callout near the edge). A boolean.

font.description: A font token (`"font.body"`) or a family name.

TTileLayer.description:
One layer of a `tiles` node. The template is resolved once per feature (and cached per tile);
inside it `d` is the feature — its properties plus `$type` (`point | line | polygon`), `$id`,
and `$x`/`$y` (its anchor point) — the signal `tile.zoom` is the zoom being drawn, and the
geometry `{"type": "feature"}` is the feature's own.

filter.description: Features to draw (an expression over `d`); all when absent.

id.description: Names the layer's nodes (default: `layer`); unique within the `tiles` node.

labels.description:
Labels: drawn above all tiles, placed in screen space in `priority` order (highest first),
dropping any that would overlap one already placed.

layer.description: The tile layer's name in the archive.

merge.description:
Batch features whose resolved style is identical into one node per tile (default true):
thousands of roads become a handful of paths. Off: one keyed node per feature.

minzoom.description: Zoom range `[minzoom, maxzoom)` in which the layer draws.

TTiles.description: A `tiles` node: which source, and how each tile layer's features become scene nodes.

layers.description: Drawn in order (later layers on top); label layers go above every tile.

tile_size.description:
The on-screen size (px) a tile should cover; the zoom follows from it. Default 512, the
size tile data is simplified for. Smaller: more detail and more tiles.

oneOf.description: A viewport with a camera. Clips to its box unless the template says `clip: false`.
One child per row (or tick, legend entry, group, number).
Vectorized marks: one prototype × the rows of a table.
A recipe from a package, expanded by the engine's sandbox.

Features of a vector-tile source, streamed for what the enclosing view shows: the engine
picks the tiles covering the view at a zoom matching the camera, and draws each tile layer's
features through a template in the enclosing `geo` coordinate system. Resolved late — per
frame, from the (possibly moving) camera — so a flight requests tiles along its path.

backdrop.description: A box drawn behind a group's content, sized to it after layout (cards, legends, tooltips).

clip.description: `"box"` clips to this node's layout box; or a rect `[x, y, w, h]`.

declutter.description:
Keeps the texts inside this group from landing on each other, once the whole scene is laid
out: in order, a text that would overlap one before it (or any other text) tries the other
side of its point — below instead of above, left instead of right, when it's offset from it
— and is left out when there's no room on either side. Place names on a map that crowd
together in a phone's narrow box; the first ones win, so list the important ones first.

dodge.description:
Places the group's content, once the whole scene is laid out, at the first of these anchors
in its box (`top-left`, `top`, `top-right`, `left`, `center`, `right`, `bottom-left`,
`bottom`, `bottom-right`; inset by the layout padding) where it covers the least data and
text — a card that never hides the bars it talks about. An anchor may be an expression (a
card that moves between states). A single anchor is a fixed place: the content goes there
whatever it covers, and never takes a band (a card over a map, where land covers everything).

id.description: Stable id for patching and provenance (optional).

key.description: The node's key: literal (`"plot"`, `["S", 3]`) or an expression over the current datum.

layout.description: How this node lays out its children in its box.

motion.description:
Motion defaults for this node and everything under it: a list of motion rules (as in the
document's `motion.rules`) scoped to the node's key path. Recipe expansion puts a recipe's
own defaults here (a line draws on, grouped bars grow). They sit under the document's
rules whatever their specificity: the document always has the last word.

pin.description:
Pinned: the origin follows cameras and scales above, the content keeps screen size. A
text's origin is its `at` (a place name stays at its map point).

scales.description: Scales declared here, visible to descendants by name.

size.description: This node's size inside its parent's layout.

when.description: Include only when this evaluates truthy.

ThemeRef.description: Which theme to use, plus the document's own token overrides and inline themes.

themes.description: Inline theme definitions (JSON as in `datars-theme`), registered before resolving `use`.

tokens.description: Document-level token overrides (honouring the theme's locks).

keys.description: Key metadata: display names and colours per key (party colours are data, not theme).

size.description: The authored size; hosts may resize (the `viewport` signal).

tables.description: Derived tables by name: a source table plus a pipeline of operations.
